profile.campus: Silicon Valley (San Jose/Santa Clara), California (Equinix's founding market, Great Oaks/Corvin/Duane campuses)
profile.address: 9 Great Oaks Boulevard, San Jose, CA 95119
profile.reading:
This building is Equinix's SV5 facility, part of Equinix's Silicon Valley data center network in the San Jose/Santa Clara area. Equinix was founded in 1998 by Al Avery and Jay Adelson, both former Digital Equipment Corporation facilities managers, on the idea of building a neutral place where competing internet networks could physically connect and exchange traffic, a model that let the company grow through network effects as more networks joined; Equinix converted to a real estate investment trust in January 2015 and trades on Nasdaq as EQIX. Silicon Valley, where Equinix is still headquartered today in nearby Redwood City, was the company's founding market, and its San Jose facilities on Great Oaks Boulevard and its Santa Clara facilities on Corvin Drive and Duane Avenue grew into one of the densest interconnection hubs in Equinix's global network as the company expanded internationally, entering Asia-Pacific in 2002, Europe via the IXEurope acquisition in 2007, Latin America in 2011, and the Middle East in 2013, and opening its 50th global data center in London by 2010 around the time it acquired Switch and Data Facilities Company. Equinix's own published specifications for the flagship SV1 building on this campus describe an 82,850-square-foot, single-story, steel-frame facility with N+1 power redundancy, a minimum cabinet density of 2kVA, 120v/208v power distribution, and generators rated for 30 hours or more at full load; Equinix markets the Great Oaks campus for its direct connections to major networks and tier-1 cloud service providers. Equinix's website did not disclose this specific building's own square footage or power capacity separately from the SV1 figure cited as representative of the broader campus.

Pacific Gas and Electric, the regional utility serving most of Silicon Valley, and Silicon Valley Power, Santa Clara's municipal utility, have both cited sustained data center load growth across the San Jose-Santa Clara-Sunnyvale corridor in their own capacity planning, a dynamic distinct from the newer data center markets elsewhere in the country given how built-out and power-constrained the Bay Area grid already is after decades of continuous data center development since Equinix's own 1998 founding in the area.

reading.body:
Equinix SV5 is a 93,495-square-foot colocation facility in San Jose, part of Equinix's Great Oaks campus, one of the densest interconnection hubs in the company's global network since the company's 1998 founding in Silicon Valley. The operator publishes no megawatt capacity figure for SV5 itself, though it confirms N+1 power redundancy and N+2 cooling redundancy, with a minimum cabinet density of 5 kilowatts per cabinet specified for this facility. The campus is marketed for direct connections to major networks and tier-1 cloud service providers.

Without published power capacity, SV5 cannot be ranked against other California facilities by raw draw; Equinix's broader Silicon Valley portfolio does not disclose individual building watts separately from its portfolio-level figures. California has 103 mapped data center facilities across the state, of which only 11 publish megawatt capacity, totaling 365 megawatts, reflecting how rarely operators disclose power specifications. SV5's contribution to California's published capacity remains unknown.

The San Jose-Santa Clara-Sunnyvale corridor where SV5 sits is already power-constrained after four decades of continuous data center development, according to capacity planning statements from Pacific Gas and Electric and Silicon Valley Power, the regional utilities. This distinguishes the site fundamentally from newer data center markets elsewhere in the country; any expansion of AI workloads here faces grid constraints distinct from land-abundant regions, making SV5's actual power allocation and available headroom critical unknowns for assessing whether this location can absorb new demand.
